# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 13 | **Condition:** moderately well preserved

---

**13:1** When all the arrows of the pit fly beyond recall and are loosed beyond hope;

**13:2** when the measuring cord falls upon judgment and the allotment of wrath upon the forsaken,

**13:3** and the outpouring of fury upon the concealed, and the season of anger upon all Belial;

**13:4** and the cords of death enclose with no escape, and the floods of Belial overflow every high bank.

**13:5** Like fire consuming all their waterways, devouring every green tree and dry from their banks,

**13:6** lashing with fiery tongues until none who draw from them remain.

**13:7** It consumes the pillars of clay and the expanse of the parched land;

**13:8** the bases of the mountains are surrendered to burning, the roots of flint become rivers of pitch.

**13:9** It devours to the great deep, and the floods of Belial burst into Abaddon,

**13:10** and the denizens of the deep cry out amid the roiling of the mire.

**13:11** The earth shrieks at the disaster come upon the world, and all its creatures wail,

**13:12** and all upon it lose their senses, staggering in the great catastrophe.

**13:13** For God thunders with the tumult of His power, and His holy habitation reverberates with His truth of glory,

**13:14** and the army of heaven raises its voice, and the eternal foundations dissolve and quake,

**13:15** and the battle of the warriors of heaven courses through the world and turns not back

**13:16** until the final consummation decreed for all ages, and nothing is comparable to it.

**13:17** I give thanks to You, O Lord, for You have ransomed my soul from the pit,

**13:18** and from Sheol-Abaddon You have lifted me to an eternal summit.

**13:19** I traverse a plain without boundary, and I know that there is hope

**13:20** for the one You fashioned from dust for the eternal assembly.

**13:21** You have cleansed the wayward spirit from great transgression, to stand in rank

**13:22** with the company of the holy ones and to enter communion with the congregation of the sons of heaven.

**13:23** You have allotted to a mortal an everlasting portion among the spirits of understanding,

**13:24** to praise Your name in communal exultation and to declare Your marvels before all Your creatures.

**13:25** As for me, a thing of clay -- what have I spoken not previously ordained,

**13:26** and what can I conceive not formerly devised? All is engraved before You

**13:27** with the pen of remembrance for every appointed time of perpetuity,

**13:28** and for the numbered periods of the age of the world in all their fixed seasons,

**13:29** and they are not concealed, and not one of them is absent from Your presence.

**13:30** How shall a man account for his sin? How shall he defend himself concerning his transgressions?

**13:31** How shall he respond to every righteous verdict? Yours, O God of knowledge, are

**13:32** all righteous works and the design of truth. But the lot of the sons of men

**13:33** is the labor of iniquity and the practice of falsehood.

**13:34** You created the breath of the tongue. You know its words and determined the fruit of the lips

**13:35** before ever they were. You set words upon a cord and the expression of breath by measure.

**13:36** You bring forth their utterances according to their mysteries and their breathings according to their calculation,

**13:37** to make Your glory known and to recount Your wonders in all Your truthful works and Your righteous judgments.

---
*LOGOS notes: Column 13 features an apocalyptic overture (lines 1-16) followed by thanksgiving (lines 17-24) and a meditation on divine foreknowledge (lines 25-37). The "floods of Belial" alludes to Psalm 18:5/2 Samuel 22:5. The deterministic theology in lines 25-29 is distinctively Qumranic.*
